_help: THE OFFER SPEC, read by bin/email_sequence.py. Copy this to specs/myoffer.json, answer it in your own words, then run: python3 bin/email_sequence.py --offer specs/myoffer.json --shape welcome --out drafts/. Keys starting with an underscore are notes and are ignored. The example filled in below is a made up chiropractor selling a made up product, so that the output reads like a real sequence instead of a form.
_why_it_is_a_file: The three sequence shapes ask for the same twelve or so facts. Answering them in a chat window means answering them again next quarter. Answering them here means the next sequence is one command.
_holes: Leave anything you do not know out. Every missing field becomes a visible [FILL: ...] hole in the drafts, with a note saying what belongs there. That is the honest outcome: the tool cannot know your refund terms or what a customer said, so it marks the gap rather than inventing a sentence for you.
_required: name, promise and audience are the only three with no sensible hole. Without them every subject line in the sequence would be a placeholder.
name: The Desk Reset
promise: Ten minutes a day that takes the ache out of your neck and shoulders by the end of the first week.
audience: people who sit at a desk for eight hours and have stopped expecting their shoulders to feel normal
_audience_short_note: Two or three words, the way you would say it in a subject line. No tool can shorten the long version above without wrecking it, so this is a separate answer.
_sender: Who signs the emails, and where a reply lands. The drafts all end with a reply invitation, so the inbox has to be one somebody reads.
_links: Real links only. A wrong link in an open email is the most expensive mistake in a launch, so anything you leave blank here becomes a hole you have to fill by hand.
_welcome_fields: Used by --shape welcome, which goes to somebody who has just paid.

access.how: Use the email address you paid with. The password came in the receipt from Stripe.

first_step: watch the four minute video called Start Here and do the first movement in it, once
stall: day three, when the morning routine collides with an early meeting and the day gets skipped
_nurture_fields: Used by --shape nurture, which goes to somebody on the list who has not bought.
objections: I have tried stretches before and they did nothing
I do not have ten minutes in the morning
surely I should see somebody in person instead
_objections_note: In their words, as close to verbatim as you can get. One email answers the first one. The rest stay here for you to rotate in when you rerun the sequence.
deliverables: Twelve movements, each filmed from two angles, none longer than ninety seconds
A ten minute morning sequence and a three minute version for the days that fall apart
One page you can print and tape to the side of your monitor
A desk setup checklist, because the chair is usually half the problem
not_for: anybody with a diagnosed disc injury or nerve pain down an arm. That needs a person in a room with you, and no video can assess it.
proof: _note: real results in real words only. Nothing here is read by the tool yet, it is where you keep the sentences you have permission to quote.
_launch_fields: Used by --shape launch. Day zero is opens_on, so the first three emails land before it. ISO dates.
_next_step_fields: Used by the last welcome email, which offers the next thing up to people who used this one.

next_step.name: The Standing Hour
next_step.promise: A six week block that rebuilds the strength the sitting took, two sessions a week.
